issue.title: rsyslog_plugin is hogging the CPU when high load is seen on rsyslog

failure.body:
#### Description

When the rsyslog is put under high load, it'll spawn multiple worker threads. Each worker thread will inturn fork a rsyslog_plugin process. The worker thread and the plugin will use a pipe on STDIN to communicate.

https://github.com/rsyslog/rsyslog/blob/1128d320750fb6cfe57b8ad53ef1d5ddf80c81cf/plugins/omprog/omprog.c#L285

```
syslog.41.gz:Apr 20 <IPV6>.143367 r-tigon-17 INFO rsyslogd: main Q:Reg: high activity - starting 1 additional worker thread(s), currently 1 active worker threads. [v8.2302.0 try https://www.rsyslog.com/e/2439 ]
syslog.41.gz:Apr 20 <IPV6>.286313 r-tigon-17 INFO rsyslogd: [origin software="rsyslogd" swVersion="8.2302.0" x-pid="8707" x-info="https://www.rsyslog.com"] rsyslogd was HUPed
syslog.40.gz:Apr 20 <IPV6>.220370 r-tigon-17 INFO rsyslogd:  message repeated 2 times: [[origin software="rsyslogd" swVersion="8.2302.0" x-pid="8707" x-info="https://www.rsyslog.com"] rsyslogd was HUPed]
```

When the load reduces, the worker thread is destroyed but the rsyslog_plugin is not killed. The write end of the pipe is also closed

```
syslog.40.gz:Apr 20 <IPV6>.220370 r-tigon-17 INFO rsyslogd:  message repeated 2 times: [[origin software="rsyslogd" swVersion="8.2302.0" x-pid="8707" x-info="https://www.rsyslog.com"] rsyslogd was HUPed]
syslog.40.gz:Apr 20 <IPV6>.227977 r-tigon-17 WARNING rsyslogd: omprog: program '/usr/bin/rsyslog_plugin' (pid 135130) did not terminate within timeout (5000 ms); ignoring it [v8.2302.0]
syslog.40.gz:Apr 20 <IPV6>.496622 r-tigon-17 WARNING rsyslogd: omprog: program '/usr/bin/rsyslog_plugin' (pid 134904) did not terminate within timeout (5000 ms); ignoring it [v8.2302.0]
syslog.40.gz:Apr 20 <IPV6>.496723 r-tigon-17 INFO rsyslogd: main Q:Reg: worker thread 55ca50b54f80 terminated, now 1 active worker threads [v8.2302.0 try https://www.rsyslog.com/e/2439 ]
```

Because the write end is closed, the getline(cin) call returns immediately. This causes rsyslog_plugin to busy wait and inturn CPU spike.
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/d3b18c40de9c1c472edfc9052d0b1de0679a31bc/src/sonic-eventd/rsyslog_plugin/rsyslog_plugin.cpp#L109

On a long running system with high rate of logs, this would lead to multiple useless rsyslog_plugin processes

#### Steps to reproduce the issue:
Generate a situation which would cause the switch to emit a lot of logs and make sure rsyslog spawns multiple threads

#### Output of `show version`:
Issue seen on master & 202311. Possible on 202305 as well

#### Potential Fix:
Ref: https://www.rsyslog.com/doc/configuration/modules/omprog.html#signalonclose

> If this switch is set to “on”, rsyslog will send a TERM signal to the child process before closing the pipe. That is, the process will first receive a TERM signal, and then an EOF on stdin.
> No signal is issued if this switch is set to “off” (default). The child process can still detect it must terminate because reading from stdin will return EOF.

We need to set signalOnClose switch to on in rsyslog config and rsyslog_plugin will recieve a SIGTERM on parent close.

rsyslog_plugin need to be updated to gracefully handle SIGTERM and exit

resolution.title: Close rsyslog plugin when rsyslog SIGTERM and EOF is sent to stream
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it
Fix #18771

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:27882794

#### How I did it

Add signalOnClose for omprog as well as close rsyslog plugin when receives an EOF.

#### How to verify it

Verify rsyslog_plugin is running inside bgp or swss container

Run `docker exec -it bgp supervisorctl restart rsyslogd`

Before change:

This will not kill current rsyslog_plugin process but instead rsyslogd will now break off its end of writing to cin and send EOF to rsyslog_plugin, however will not send a signal SIGTERM or SIGKILL to rsyslog_plugin. Therefore, rsyslog plugin will run in an infinite loop forever, constantly calling getline raising CPU to 100% inside docker.

After change of adding signalOnClose="on" to conf file inside omprog, rsyslogd will now send SIGTERM to rsyslog_plugin process running inside container, and rsyslog_plugin will die.

? (         ): rsyslog_plugin/578637  ... [continued]: read())                                             = -1 (unknown) (INTERNAL ERROR: strerror_r(512, [buf], 128)=22)
